M O R E   M A I L ! !
  December, 1991     Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Ray Barnes...........03    04

 Dennis Turton........05    07

 Malcolm Perry........11    18

 Stephen Watson.......19    22

 Damian Griffiths.....23    28

 (TO) John Cleveland.. -    37

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

    From: Ray Barnes, WESTBURY
Thank you for the last batch of
back numbers.An article in No.42
on monitor wiring by Cliff
Jackson took my eye. He seems to
overcome the problem of intens-
ity(BRIGHT)on his 128 but please
how do you overcome it on a +3?

I run a Commodore 1084s monitor
(Phillips badged) with the +3
which has the same input lines
as the monitor described in the
article and also I can't get
BRIGHT since there doesn't seem
to be an intensity line coming
out of the +3. Can I find an
intensity line somewhere in the
+3 or have I made a wrong guess
by assuming the RGB signals from
the computer are TTL and not
linear?            - Ray Barnes

To Ray Barnes from Brian Gaff

I don't think the +3 or +2A have
any facilities for BRIGHT. It is
probably possible to do it, if
you had the circuit but it would
mean fiddling about inside and I
personally would not bother.

Your second question set me
thinking. I had always assumed
the RGB output was TTL, as the
128K and +2 were. However, I do
not know this for sure. It would
explain the missing BRIGHT lead,
if it turned out to be analogue!

Perhaps someone has tried using
the +3 on an analogue RGB monit-
or and can let us know if BRIGHT
works. In the meantime, I shall
make some enquiries!     - B.G.

From Dennis A. Turton, LIVERPOOL

 RE: STANDING ORDERS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

What an excellent 50th edition
of OUTLET. Congratulations!

Now down to business. In your
letter to me in the form of an
ORDER FORM, you state that the
Standing Order charge is `3.50
per issue. My question is, is
this the price for the Spectrum
+3 disk version? If it is then
please send me a Standing Order
Form right away!

If this is right, how do you do
it for that price?

Whilst on the subject of Order
Forms, what fonts or program did
you use to obtain the lettering
that you use to produce the form
i.e, the heading at the top of
the form?I am also interested in
how the boxes are drawn,assuming
they were drawn on a Spectrum.
If this was not the case, do you
have such a program that will
draw lines across and down the
page? For example, designing and
drawing charts,e.g.,time tables.
I'm sure other people would find
this kind of utility very
useful.

Well, Ron & Brian, keep up the
brilliant work and here's to the
100th edition in December 1995!
                 - Dennis Turton

Brian Cavers to Dennis Turton

I'm afraid the +3 version of
OUTLET is NOT `3.50 by standing
order as you say: IT'S ONLY `3!!
Look carefully again at the form
and you will see all versions
are the same except microdrive.

Yes, `3 for the +3 version of
OUTLET is unbelievable isn't it?
You can still pay `4 for a blank
3"disc in some High Street shops
so how do we do it? By buying 3"
discs in bulk we can get them
for under `2. Remember, High St.
shops exist primarily for profit
with the customer as a means to
that end. We work the other way
round to produce something we
think is worthwhile and provide
a service with profit secondary.

It's a funny old world though.In
this same issue is a letter from
another reader, Marc Broster,who
rarely buys OUTLET because "at
`2 I don't think it's very good
value.", he says. Marc must have
bought an odd issue at one of
the All-Format Fairs where we
sell OUTLET at a ludicrous `2 so
he assumes that's the regular
price.I hope everyone will still
write to me at the funny farm
when they come to take me away.

Anyway, by now you should have
received the standing order form
Dennis. As for the order form,it
is done by a commercial printer
which accounts for the quality.
To integrate boxes and lines
with text you really need PCG'S
DTP package...

This comprises WORDMASTER,a word
processor, HEADLINER, a graphic
and title designer and TYPELINER
the "desktop publisher". They're
available separately or together
as follows...

           +D/DISCIPLE  +3/TAPE

 WORDMASTER   `13.95    `15.95

 HEADLINER    `10.95    `12.95

 TYPELINER    `18.95    `20.95

 ALL THREE    `37.95    `39.95


Free U.K. delivery from P.C.G.,
61 School Street, Barrow-in-
Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW

However, I note what you say
about drawing charts etc. and
these are usually programs that
are special to one task. For
instance we had a bar chart pro-
gram in Issue 50 called HI-BAR
and there's a graph chart soon
in a future issue. If you can
specify a particular task in
more detail then a reader may be
able to take on the project. If
simple, like HI-BAR, I may find
time myself. It should not be
too difficult to do something
like a timetable.

                        - Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER


Re: All Format Show, Birmingham.

November 10th gave a choice:stay
at home for roast lunch and
watch Batman on TV or spend `4
(`3 if your Format arrived in
time) and visit the show. I had
made my mind up I was not going
but 11 AM sunday I decided
otherwise. Suffice to say I was
back in time to see Batman and
ate my packed lunch at home.

It should have been called "All
Formats Except Spectrum"!O.K.,to
be fair there were the odd
Spectrum bits and pieces if you
looked hard enough.

General hardware such as discs,
labels, paper, ribbons etc., in
ample supply and prices between
cheap and not-so-cheap. There
were plenty of various firms
showing off their computers and
bags of software for all but
Spectrums. Empty tables were
conspicious by their numbers.

However on the Spectrum/Sam
scene Samco was represented
selling games and the usual sam
utilities with a Sam box on
display but no Sam in sight. I
would have thought a demo and
try-out of the games being sold
would have,at least,been a must
(perhaps they had such a rush in
the morning they had sold the
demo model by midday!!!).

FORMAT had the usual stand. SAM
SUPPLEMENT and ZAT were demon-
strating their discs on Sams and
that was all I spotted! There
were odd +2's,+3's and Interface
1's to be found but not much
else was seen of interest. You
could buy a +2 circuit and
service booklet for `5 but I had
bought mine the week before at a
radio show for only `2.My journ-
ey was not a total loss as I
managed to replace my bottle of
disc-cleaning fluid that had
evaporated into thin air 'cos I
did not put the top back on
properly, for 50p (only seen in
packs with disc before). I also
got a 6-way Centronics automatic
printer switch that was sorely
needed when running four systems
and only having a 2-way switch.

I can strongly recommend auto-
matic switches when running
multiple computers and only one
printer (PSST.... anybody wanna
buy a 2-way?).

When I arrived about midday it
was quite crowded in the halls
but an hour later it had thinned
out quite a bit. I possibly
missed some "bargains" by not
getting there earlier but from
the type of stalls present I
would not think much in my line.

If you are reading this then
your interests most likely would
not have been catered for. On
top of this the poor way this
aspect of computing was suported
by traders would not be too
likely to gain new recruits.

Say someone was thinking of a
computer. They would see a
couple of Sams with a disc demo/
mag. and little else related
with Sam. Brand x has many
stalls with working computers
showing off their wares with a
fair selection of software and
hardware. Which is going to draw
the most interest? Which is
going to make people stop and
look? a box with a picture of
SAM or a number of working
computers running both serious
programs, demos and games?

I think part of the problem is
the entrance fee is too high.
This reflects on attendance and
so dealers do not consider it
worthwhile going.

At this type of show,rather than
each product-supplier having
their own space, would it not be
be better to book say,six tables
and then all Spectrum and Sam
products would be put on show.


Suppliers could take turns to
man the combined effort display.
O.K., so Mr X might whinge at
selling Mr Y's competitive
product but in the long run
prospective users would at least
see there is more to Sam than
two disc mags and a few games
and that Spectrums are still
well supported.

This would benefit all in the
long run.

Amateur radio-type shows are
mainly put on by local clubs. I
wonder if this idea would work
for computers with Sam and
Spectrum dealers working with
local clubs to put on a show?
This would ease the problems of
small supporters of the Sam and
Spectrum (which really covers a
fair proportion of software and
hardware suppliers) who would
not then have the full expense
of a stand and have to be tied
up manning stands at each show.

This column has been as inform-
ative and interesting on the
latest developments and up-and-
coming-items for the Spectrum
and Sam as the Birmingham
computer show was! All I can say
is, "Sorry!!".   - Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcom Perry

We have difficulty finding time
to attend these fairs and we're
not encouraged by the attendance
of SAM and Spectrum users or at
least, the inability to know
which fairs may be well-attended
and which not.

It's not too bad for the box-
shifters who don't need to speak
much but we could talk ourselves
hoarse for 20 or 30 minutes
demonstrating say, OUTLET or
OUTWRITE for a sale of only `2
or `8 respectively. This is not
really economic except as promo-
tion so it becomes more and more
of an effort to go when we have
so many pressing tasks to do in
the production of OUTLET. -Brian

From Stephen Watson, E. KILBRIDE

It is with much regret I must
say this is my last communicat-
ion to you; I have succumbed to
the"Industry Standard"and bought
myself a portable PC.

I would like to say before I go
how much I have enjoyed OUTLET
over the past few years. Being a
User of utilities with very lim-
ited programming experience and
little hardware knowledge I have
always found OUTLET informative
and interesting; not an issue
has gone by without something to
catch my eye.May I wish you much
success in the future and if you
ever decide on a PC version you
have my address to send a sub-
scription form!

This does mean of course I have
a SPECTRUM 128K+ with a Plus D
for sale,along with a disc drive
that probably needs servicing
and a Brother HR5 printer
together with back issues of
OUTLET and FORMAT and some games
and utilities on tape. It's all
original and had fairly light
use. If anyone is interested
send an SAE to the above address
for a list or give me a call
between 5 and 6pm on 03552 29187
- all reasonable offers consid-
ered.

Note that I am able to deliver
to some areas of Scotland and
the North East of England and my
terms are cash only (or rather
my Bank Manager's are!!!!!!!).

Thanks once again for OUTLET and
long may you continue to grow.

     Regards - Steve Watson.

P.S. Anyone interested in moving
to a P.C., I bought an Amstrad
PPC640D, widely advertised in
such publications as Micro Mart,
and, I might add, widely slagged
off in the more serious PC maga-
zines. However,it does have twin
720K, 3.5" drives and a built-in
Hayes compatible modem and all
for under `300! Admittedly the
LCD screen is not brilliant but,
with due respect to the"serious"
magazines I couldn't find any
other portable with the same
spec, for the same money - few,
if any, other portables have
built in modems.    more!...

Just one point to note:like mine
these models tend to be of the
"grey" import variety but if you
shop around - unlike me - some
of the companies are offering
on-site maintenance for an extra
`30.00 which may give you rather
more peace of mind. For those
looking for printers I also
picked up an Amstrad DMP 4000
printer for `100 plus vat. I'm
not going to advertise any
companies here, all I'll say is
"see press for details".



Many thanks, Steve - and good
luck!
                         - Brian

From: D. Griffiths,
      55 Rickmansworth Rd,
      Watford, Herts., WD1 7HS

Dear Ron and Brian,

May I ask you to print my full
address so people can write to
me concerning my letter.

When writing long program lines
(say from 10 lines up to a full
screen length), I often find
that the computer (+3) chops off
the end. Is this due to memory
limitations or something, and is
there a maximum line length,
because the computer varies in
its acceptance of lines; some-
times it'll accept 12 lines,
other times only eight!

I want a decent D.T. Publishing
pack to use with my printer, a
"Star LC24-200". Have you, or
any readers any suggestions? Is
the Desk Top Publishing pack
from "P.C.G." any good?

(Re:'WordMaster','Headliner' and
'Typeliner'), would I need all
three programs or just Typeliner
(i.e. the D.T.P. part)?

I've a "Multiface 3" for my
Spectrum+3, but I am having
difficulty using it to do screen
dumps. I've a Star LC24-200
Printer, and although occasion-
ally I've succeeded, 99% of the
time I just get garbage printed,
or simply linefeeds! (Even with
the help of the instructions!)

What is CP/M, and CP/M Software?

I've a large collection of
tunes, games, utilities, etc,
for the Spectrum, and thought
that Outlet readers might be
interested in them. - They are
all for sale very cheaply; For
example, around 40p, provided
you (the reader) supplies a +3
Disk, (NOT +D, Opus, etc,) or a
cassette, along with an S.A.E.
(Very Important)! Also send an
S.A.E. for details. I also have
quite a large selection of
Spectrum games for sale. (All
originals, both old and new, and
some without boxes). Ranging
from as little as 30p up to a
couple of pounds). Send an SAE
for details and price list.

Finally, I have a whole load of
Multiface Pokes available, again
free,except for the S.A.E.(Write
to me for details on all above.)

Do OUTLET readers know of any
Speccy "Public Domain" Libaries?

Would you like any more Cross-
words (Via "Procross")?

I want to start writing decent
adventures, preferably ones with
graphics as well, can you name
the best.(e.g.,'Quill', 'Paw')?

Readers might be interested in a
Spectrum Software Hire Club.
I've just joined and I am quite
impressed.You hire the software,
usually for 1/2 weeks, and costs

as little as `1/2, including PP.
They have a wide selection of
games and also utilities, e.g.,
Tasman programs, music programs,
databases, etc. Write to:
Spectrum Software Club,
32, Dursley Road, TrowBridge,
Wiltshire, BA14 0NW

Finally three slightly personal
questions:

a) How old  are  you two?

b) How come  nothing  seems to
be by Ron, incl. letter replies,
programs,etc. Does he mainly
Compile "OUTLET" or something?

c) Is "OUTLET" a hobby, or a
full time job as it were?
             - Damian Griffiths

Brian Cavers to Damian Griffiths

In 48K mode there is no limit to
BASIC line length in theory but
in practice when you have filled
the screen then,although you can
still type more on line,a 'rasp'
or warning buzz sounds at each
keypress drastically slowing it
down. However,this can be almost
silenced with POKE 23608,0 and
you can also type the last part
of the line first and the first
part last (otherwise you are
typing blindly as the cursor is
off the bottom of the screen).
The easy way is to use LINEZIP
(OUTLET 2)to join lines together
but you would have to get the
tape version, of course, as it's
not available on +3 disc.

In +3 BASIC, the limit is,as you
note, rather variable, as the
128K BASIC editor is rather iffy
and is not the best environment
to work in. If you want to enter
a large line you could enter:
SPECTRUM to get 48K, enter the
line(s) and then RANDOMIZE USR
23354 to get back to 128K (so
long as you've not used any
printer commands).


I don't use 128K BASIC often as
I dislike the editor intensely
because of its many quirks but I
would have thought you could get
more than 12 lines reliably but
it won't surprise me if you
can't! Has anyone else noticed
this flaw?

PCG's DTP pack is the only one
to consider. It's difficult to
get started with but the results
are good. You really need the
whole package. "TYPELINER" and
"HEADLINER" are "sub-programs"of
"WORDMASTER" and load into it.As
far as I know they cannot be
used separately and,in any case,
they would limit your operations
to certain areas, such as large
text.

I got off to a bad start with
PCG's DTP because it takes time
to get to understand, the manual
is not as helpful as it could be
and I lacked time and the micro-
drive I was using had some bugs
which drove me crazy in the end!
Anyone else care to comment?

I do not have a Multiface 3. I
wasn't even aware that it gave
printer dumps!Check your printer
manual to see if the STAR has a
special graphics mode that must
be switched in or, conversely,an
IBM mode or some other mode that
must be switched out! I assume
that the Multiface 3 does not
need any special initializing
from BASIC before use?(unlikely)

CP/M is software that interfaces
between the computer and normal
user programs enabling software
that is written for CP/M to run
on any computer with CP/M. It
calls the particular computer's
own routines to carry out the
standard CP/M features such as
text printing or calculations,
etc.

The advantage of CP/M is that
there is a lot of software about
and most of it will run on any
computer with CP/M. The weakness
is that it uses the simplest of
routines and does not use the
very best features specific to
each particular computer, for
example, there are no high-res
graphics at all. With the +3 in
particular there is also the
problem that most CP/M software
is on 5.25" or 3.5" discs and
needs conversion.There is a
great deal already on 3" though
and, I believe, it only needs a
3.5" "B" drive to get at the
rest. Another plus is that a lot
of the CP/M software is PD, that
is, in the public domain, and so
extremely inexpensive.

There's a new advert in this
month's OUTBOARD for PROPAC PD,
a Spectrum public domain library
and there's also Sinclair and
SAM Computing magazine which has
a PD section. Write to 57 Lovers
Walk, Dunstable, Beds, LU5 4BG.
However, since the magazine was
launched earlier this year their
service has been unreliable due
to being unable to cope with the
demand. The last I heard was
that things should be improving
but I have not yet seen any
evidence of this so cannot give
my unreserved recommendation
until I hear more from satisfied
customers! You can but try! Send
an SAE I suggest. I think you
will probably have to subscribe
to the magazine though to get
the PD!

I must add here that the few PD
libraries that have come and
gone for the Spectrum have often
had a high proportion of OUTLET
PD software as we were probably
the first (only?)to CONSISTENTLY
PRODUCE and PUBLISH original PD
software (as against merely
"acquiring" PD from others and
then reselling t to the public).
It's likely that 20 or 30% of
all known Spectrum PD (there are
not huge amounts anyway!) may be
OUTLET FREEWARE!

I have heard of other libraries
but they seem to have faded away
as the market is not large and
they are mostly run by amateur
enthusiasts. I keep my eyes open
though!

Yes, please send crosswords for
PROCROSS! Like all contributions
to OUTLET we pay a modest amount
for any published.

PAW is definitely the best text
and graphics adventure writing
utility for the Spectrum. It's
only drawback is that it has so
many features and so much flexi-
bility that it is not easy to
grasp. However, anyone applying
themselve can produce quite a
professional result given time
and patience.

I'm in my mid-forties and Ron a
little older. I edit and compile
the magazine at present,Ron runs
the "business" side, processing
orders, keeping accounts etc.

I work full-time on OUTLET but
Ron "only" does about 35 hours a
week on it in his spare time.No,
I can't say what I do is really
full-time as I steal 20 minutes
sometimes for meals and even
sleep at night occasionally.

Finally, note that, if you are
offering to copy software on to
others' +3 discs it must be your
own copyright or PD. If so, why
not contribute it to OUTLET? It
will reach more users and we pay
a modest amount for each item,
typically `3 to `10 each.However
it MUST be your own work or PD
or you are not entitled to even
give it away (except for the
original as second-hand).
                        - Brian.

  Chris Pile to John Cleveland
[in reply to last month's query]

Well, I am sorry to say it isn't
possible to get CP/M, or indeed,
ANY bootable program to boot
from an ULTRA 208 format disk.

When I say ANY bootable program,
this doesn't include programs
that "boot" using the DISK basic
program,just programs that actu-
ally boot via the boot sector at
track 0, sector 0.This boot sec-
tor doesn't exist on 208k disks.

This is an offshoot of the 208k
method. It's typical computer
compromise!!! You can never have
all things all the time; sacri-
fices have to be made!!

Another word on the 208 format:
Again, because of the way it
works,you can't do an ERASE *.*,
because the DPB (disk parameter
block) is treated as a file and
because this "file" is essential
it is software write-protected.
So, any erasing on a 208k disk
has to be done explicitly on the
individual files.

I'm afraid I can't comment on
Kobrasoft's DICE program. I have
never seen it. What I can say,
however, is that it must be
assuming that the disk directory
etc., is always at a certain
position on the disk,this is not
true and would probably explain
why the 208k format trips it up.
                         Chris.

Well, I am sorry to say it isn't possible to get CP/M, or indeed, ANY bootable program to boot from an ULTRA 208 format disk.

В режиме 48K теоретически нет предела длине строки BASIC, но на практике, когда вы заполняете экран, хотя вы всё ещё можете продолжать ввод, при каждом нажатии клавиши звучит дребезжащий предупреждающий зуммер, сильно замедляющий процесс. Впрочем, его можно практически заглушить с помощью POKE 23608,0, а также можно сначала ввести конец строки, а начало — в последнюю очередь (иначе придётся печатать вслепую, так как курсор уйдёт за нижний край экрана). Самый простой способ — использовать LINEZIP (OUTLET 2) для склеивания строк, но вам, разумеется, понадобится кассетная версия, так как на диске для +3 её нет.

В +3 BASIC ограничение, как вы заметили, довольно плавающее, поскольку редактор 128K BASIC весьма капризен и представляет собой не самую удобную среду для работы. Если вам нужно ввести огромную строку, можно набрать SPECTRUM для перехода в 48K, ввести строку (или строки), а затем сделать RANDOMIZE USR 23354 для возврата в 128K (при условии, что вы не использовали команды принтера).

Я не часто пользуюсь 128K BASIC, так как терпеть не могу этот редактор из-за множества его причуд, но мне казалось, что больше 12 строк ввести всё-таки можно без сбоев — хотя я не удивлюсь, если это не так! Кто-нибудь ещё замечал этот изъян?

DTP-пакет от PCG — единственный, на который стоит обратить внимание. Начать работать с ним непросто, но результаты получаются хорошими. Вам действительно нужен весь комплект. «TYPELINER» и «HEADLINER» — это «подпрограммы» для «WORDMASTER» и загружаются непосредственно в него. Насколько мне известно, по отдельности они работать не могут, да и в любом случае это ограничило бы ваши возможности лишь отдельными задачами вроде крупного текста.

У меня с DTP от PCG поначалу не заладилось: требуется время, чтобы во всём разобраться, руководство пользователя могло бы быть и понятнее, времени мне не хватало, а используемый микродрайв вдобавок выдавал ошибки, что в конце концов довело меня до белого каления! Кто-нибудь ещё хочет высказаться по этому поводу?

У меня нет Multiface 3. Я даже не знал, что он умеет делать дампы экрана на принтер! Загляните в руководство к принтеру: возможно, у STAR есть специальный графический режим, который необходимо включить, или, наоборот, режим IBM или какой-то другой, который нужно отключить! Полагаю, Multiface 3 не требует специальной инициализации из BASIC перед использованием? (Вряд ли).

CP/M — это системное программное обеспечение, выступающее прослойкой между компьютером и обычными пользовательскими программами, позволяя софту, написанному под CP/M, работать на любом компьютере с этой ОС. Она вызывает собственные подпрограммы конкретного компьютера для выполнения стандартных функций CP/M, таких как вывод текста на печать, вычисления и т.д.

Преимущество CP/M в том, что под неё существует масса программ, и большинство из них запустится на любой машине с CP/M. Слабая сторона — использование простейших стандартных процедур без задействования лучших уникальных возможностей конкретного компьютера; к примеру, там напрочь отсутствует графика высокого разрешения. В случае с +3 возникает дополнительная проблема: большинство программ CP/M распространяется на дискетах 5.25" или 3.5" и требует конвертации. Впрочем, много софта уже есть и на 3" дисках, а для доступа к остальному, как я понимаю, достаточно подключить 3.5" дисковод «B». Ещё один плюс — огромное количество CP/M-софта является PD (Public Domain, общественным достоянием) и стоит сущие копейки.
